I have been farming these 2.6 mu of chili for 40 years. I am 57 now, and I never went to school, but I know this land with my hands and my eyes. Last year my chili did alright — I got about 4,000 jin per mu. This year I will do mostly the same, because change is risky and I cannot afford a bad year. My neighbor Lao Zhang used a little more fertilizer last year and his chili looked bigger, so I will add a bit more too. Better to spend a little extra on fertilizer than to lose the whole crop.

I will rotavate the field first, like I always do. Then I will buy seedlings from the market in town — the kind I bought last year, the red ones. I plant about 4,000 plants per mu. For the 2.6 mu, I need to buy enough for that. For fertilizer, I will put down three bags of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer — that is 50 kilograms each, so about one bag per mu roughly, spread before I lay the plastic mulch. Then when the plants flower, I will topdress with two more bags of urea, and I will also add one bag of potassium fertilizer because Lao Zhang said his chili got redder when he did that. I irrigate from my well. When the soil looks dry and the leaves start to droop, I water. Last year I watered five times, and this year I think I will do the same, maybe six if it is very dry. For bugs, I spray when I see them. I keep some insecticide and fungicide at home. Last year I sprayed about ten times in total. I would rather spray one extra time than let the aphids ruin everything. I work the field myself and my husband helps. We do not hire anyone — 2.6 mu is small, we can manage.
